notes: Name: In his 1835 birth entry he is registered under his Jewish name, Hirschel Löbel. Moravian Jews at the time commonly had a Jewish name (used in synagogue and often in the registers) and a German name for civil life, usually chosen to sound like it or share its first letter. Hirsch/Hirschel/Herschel was very commonly rendered as Heinrich (Löbel/Löw usually as Leopold). By the 1860s, when his own children were registered, families used the German names, so as an adult he appears as Heinrich. The match rests on: father Bernard Mondschein, the same household (house no. 144), and a birth date consistent with his age (53) at death in 1888.
Death date: Geni gives 6 Aug 1888; the Kyjov death register (kn 939) gives 26 May 1888, aged 53, used here.

(Gruntovní kniha židovských domů 19–155, SOkA Hodonín, AM Kyjov, Nro. 144 Brantweinhaus, fol. 151v–152 | 1860: "nach der am 16. März 1855. verstorbenen Fanni Mondschein, wird das Eigenthumsrecht für die erblasserischen Söhne: Mondschein Heinrich und Gerson beide minderjährig im Werthe zu 6575. Gulden österr. Währ. einverleibt." | "Gemäß des Kaufvertrages d. Gaya am 22. Juli 1859. geschlossen zwischen Rudolf Kämpf und den am 7 Juli 1859 N. 3895 et 4332 für großjährig erklärten Brüdern Heinrich und Gerson Mondschein, wird auf dieses Brantweinhaus und den Keller fol. 110. das Eigenthumsrecht für Kämpf Rudolf in Kunewald um den Preis zu 5775 Gulden österr. Währ. einverleibt.", eingetragen 24. September 1860)

Birth year: the 20 Apr 1848 birth previously recorded here belongs to her sister Jetti (Henriette); the 1848 entry (kn 932, p. 7) reads 'Jetti Redlich'. Netti's age at marriage in May 1862 (22 y 4 m) puts her birth about Jan 1840; Geni gives 1839.

links.page: Indication sketch, Kyjov (Gaya), owner list: no. XX, Redlich Lazar, house no. 176a
links.summary: The owner list of the Stable Cadastre indication sketch for Kyjov (Gaya) names Lazar Redlich as owner no. XX, with house no. 176a; the next owner, no. XXI, is Emanuel Fischer with house no. 176b — the other half of the same house. The Fischer name fits Lazar's wife Chani née Fischer; Emanuel may be a relative of hers. Owners entered with '0' had no house. Lazar was born in 1818, so this owner list was kept up to date after the 1827 survey (the struck-through entry numbers also show later revision); it reflects ownership from about the 1840s, not 1827. Read from James's screenshot, 18 Nov 2026. Note: the 1848 birth of Lazar's daughter Jetti (Henriette) is recorded at house no. 167 — possibly the same house with the digits transposed (176), worth checking.

C.M. richtig verkauft … 3tens … willigt Benedikt Mareczek, daß der Hausantheil No 137 dem Kläger Bernard Mondschein nach Berichtigung des Kaufschillings zu 500 fl. C.Mz. grundbücherlich … zugeschrieben werden könne …" · [clauses 2 and 4, read from James's full-page image] "2tens In Verbindung mit diesem Kauf- eigentlich Vergleichsgeschäfte stehet eine Forderung des Beklagten an den Kläger, worüber sie gegenseitig … dahin einig geworden sind, daß … Kläger dem Beklagten noch 117 fl. 21 kr.? schuldig ist, und sich verbindlich macht, diesen Betrag in einem Monath a dato ohne Zögerung bey Executions-Vermeidung zu bezahlen." · "4tens Hat sich Beklagter Benedict Mareczek den unter dem verkauften Hausantheile befindlichen Keller auf beiläufige 400? … eigenthümlich vorbehalten …" (continues on the next scan, not yet read). notes: Mehlhändler zu Gaya

Flour dealer (Mehlhändler) in Gaya; Familiant as a later-born son (Nachgeborener). Married Ernestine Schiff by permission of 27 May 1838. No parents on Geni; several children were born in house no. 150, the house where Gerson Bernard Mondschein died in 1835 and his wife Verona Dwora in 1843, which suggests he was their son.
(Jewish house land register, house 144 continued, fol. 152v–153: Benedikt Mareczek heirs 1837 – Moyses, Elias?, Leopold?, Josefa, Ernestina?, no Mathias)

(Gruntovní kniha židovských domů 19–155, Nro 150, fol. 181v–182 | Mondschein Mathias: "de praes. 2. Oktober resol. 5. Oktbr 1833. N. 1492. Jud. Derselbe hat das Eigenthum dieses Judenhauses auf Grund der Schenkungs?urkunde seines Vaters Bernard Mondschein dto 1. intab. 5. Oktober 1833. N. 1492. Jud. erworben im Werthe von … Conv. 400. Vide U. L. Tom II. fol. 266. et pr." | 1833: Schätzungsurkunde dto 19. Oktober 1833 N. 1540, Werth 322 | Dawid Herschl Sonnenschein "hat dieses Judenhaus laut des Kontrakts dto 8. Februar intab 2. April 1842. N. 549. Jud. von Mathias Mondschein erkauft um … Conv. 500" | Basis for his parentage: father = Gerson Bernard, owner of house 150 since 1800, d. 1835; mother not named.)

Parentage research: House 150 in Gaya was bought by Bernard Mondschein from the Jewish community on 7 Sept 1800, given to Mathias by deed of his father Bernard on 1 Oct 1833, sold by Mathias to David Herschel Sonnenschein in 1842, and bought by Nathan Redlich in 1846. Mathias still lived at house 150 when he married in 1838, and moved to house 19, bought 1842-43. His father is therefore Gerson Bernard Mondschein, c.1767-1835, not Bernard junior, who was born 1798. This fits his Familianten entry Nachgeb., a later-born son, and his trade as a flour dealer like Gerson Bernard in 1807. The deed does not name his mother; Verona is assumed. The births of Mathias Mandl, 22 Jun 1806, son of Moyses Mandl, and Mathias Moritschek, 23 May 1807, son of Benedikt, are not his; Mathias Mareczek is also absent from Benedikt's 1837 heirs.

links.summary: Elias Fischer pledges his house shares No. 19 and 21 as security ("Hypothek") for 620 fl. C.M. that the Familianten Jakob Mandl and Jakob Kaufmann? owe under a sub-lease ("Subarendirungs-Contract") for the army supply depot ("k.k. Magazin") feeding the 2nd squadron of the Emperor Franz cuirassier regiment; bond dated Gaya 6 April 1826, registered 8 April 1826 (N. 309 Jud.). Margin note: the charge for 332? fl. was cleared ("gelöscht") by the magistrate's order of 10 May 1828
links.transcript: "Fischer Elias." · "No 309 Jud." · "Das […]amt hat beiliegende Verschreibungsurkunde, da das Elias Fischer auf seine Hausantheile No 19 und 21 zu intabuliren und sie dem Jakob Mandl zu seinem Gebrauche hinauszugeben. Gaya den 8ten April 1826. Franz Robolsky m.p. Bürgermeister" · "Ich Endesgefertigter bekenne durch gegenwärtige Urkunde, daß, falls die hiesigen Familianten Jakob Mandl und Jakob Kaufmann? aus dem Ihnen … k.k. Magazin auf den zur Verpflegung des Obristlieutenants 2ten Escadron des E.H. Franz Cuirassier Regiments angeschlossenen Subarendirungs-Contract den ihnen zugeführten Geldvorschuß von 620 fl. C.M. erhalten sollten, ich für diesen Vorschuß von Sechs Hundert und Zwanzig Gulden Conv: Münz mit meinem gesammten Vermögen, insbesondere aber mit meinen beiden schuldenfreyen Häusern No 19 und 21 dergestalt haften wolle, daß falls dieser Vorschuß während der Dauer des Contracts von besagten Contrahenten nicht ganz eingebracht werden könnte, ich dem höchsten Aerario jeden Abgang aus meinem eigenen Vermögen zu vergütten schuldig seyn solle. Ich bestelle daher zur Hypothek meine freyeigenen zwey Häuser und …, die Mall … diese gegenwärtige Urkunde zur Erlangung der Sicherheit auf dieselben intabulirt werde. Zur Bestättigung dessen ist meine eigene und zweyer erbethenen Zeugen eigenhändige Unterschrift. Gaya den 6ten April 1826. Elias Fischer m.p." · margin: "Auf Ansuchen … Anordnung des löbl. Magistrats vom 10ten May 828 sind 332 fl. … gelöscht. Gaya den 10ten May 828"

CMz hat der Käufer Elias Fischer Achtzig Gulden CMz zu Handen des Verkäufers Moses Herschl Hayek gleich bar bezahlt …"

links.summary: Exchange contract ("Tauschkontrakt") of 7 Sept 1800 between Bernard Mondschein and the Jewish community: Bernard gives his own small house ("Häusel") No. 151 to the community for use as its hospital ("Spital"), and takes in exchange the community's house No. 150, with its rights and burdens; copied here as an extract, recorded by magistrate's order of 24 Jan 1818 (N. 83 Jud.). Further lines: a debt of 100 fl. on the house; the community elders sign. This is the original "Kontrakt vom 7 Sept. 800" cited in F93
links.transcript: "Bernard Mondschein · Extract" · "Heute zu Ende gesetzten Tag und Jahr ist zwischen dem Bernard Mondschein an einem, dann den Vorstehern der hiesigen Judengemeinde … nachstehender Tauschkontrakt errichtet und zu Stande gebracht worden. 1tens Übergibt Bernard Mondschein sein Häusel No 151, welches er bis itzt eigenthümlich besessen hat, zum … Eigenthume der hiesigen Gemeinde zum Spital …" · (right page) "… das von der Gemeinde eingetauschte Häusel No 150 sammt Gärtl? … die Gefahr und Lasten des Häusels No 151 übernimmt. Zur Sicherheit dieses Tauschkontrakts hat man es in dem Grundbuche einzutragen. Zur Bestättigung dessen haben sich beide Theile eigenhändig gefertigt. Gaya am 7ten 7bris 800." · signed "Bernard Mondschein" and the community elders · head note "Zufolge Anordnung des löbl. Magistrats vom 24ten Jänner 818 sub No 83 Jud. … auf das Judenhaus No 150 zur Vormerkung bewilligt"

links.summary: Marriage of Heinrich Luchesi, confectioner in Neutitschein, 32, single, and Augusta Holleschek, 22, single, on 18 August 1885 in Neutitschein (Nový Jičín). Groom's parents: Josef Luchesi, burgher of Weißkirchen (Hranice), and Marie née Alexander. Bride's parents: Johann Holleschek, master butcher, and Rosalia née Neußer. The groom's baptism certificate came from the parish of Keltsch (Kelč), so Heinrich was born there about 1853. Bride was a minor; her father gave consent in person. A second Luchesi (first name read as Samuel, of Vienna) was a witness.

links.label: Ad by a Luchesi of Meidling (Vienna), Hauptstraße 36, 1889 — same address as the 1885 wedding witness
links.source: Neues Wiener Tagblatt (ANNO code nwg), newspaper
links.summary:
Advertisement (no. 4194, 28 Apr 1889): an old, well-known freight-forwarding business with a wholesale and retail coal trade in a larger industrial town in Moravia is for sale immediately on very favourable terms 'because of family circumstances'; enquiries to Luchesi, Meidling (Vienna), Hauptstraße 36.

Why it is attached here: the witness at Heinrich Luchesi's 1885 wedding in Neutitschein was read as '[Samuel?] Luchesi, [Privatbeamter?] Wien, [Mariahilf?] Hauptstr. 36'; this ad shows the address is almost certainly Meidling, Hauptstraße 36, so the same Vienna Luchesi (a close relative of Josef Jr and Heinrich, exact relationship unknown) lived there 1885–1889. The ad is NOT evidence of Josef Jr's death: it gives 'family circumstances', no estate/heirs/widow wording, the contact is in Vienna, and Josef Jr was alive in Feb 1889 as town secretary with no known link to a freight or coal business.
links.transcript:
Neues Wiener Tagblatt, 28. April 1889, S. 36, Anzeige Nr. 4194

Altes renommirtes Speditions- mit Engros- und Detail-Kohlengeschäft ist in einer größeren Provinz- und industrie-reichen Stadt Mährens wegen Familienverhältnissen unter sehr günstigen Verhältnissen sofort zu verkaufen. Nähere Auskunft ertheilt Luchesi, Meidling, Hauptstraße 36.

links.source: Matriky Hranice (Mährisch Weißkirchen), Římskokatolická fara Hranice (FamilySearch images)
links.summary: Anna Maria Luchesi, legitimate daughter, born and baptised 20 May 1846 in Mährisch Weißkirchen (Hranice), house no. 404, by chaplain Fr. Bayer. Father Joseph Luchesi, owner of the shooting range (Schießstattbesitzer) in Weißkirchen. Mother Maria, daughter of Franz Tambour, burgher of the town, and Katharina. Godparents were the maternal grandparents, who signed with crosses (+++). Note: later records (1886–1893) name Heinrich Luchesi's mother as Marie née Alexander, so this Maria Tambour is either an earlier wife of Josef or this Joseph is a different (older) Luchesi.

links.label: Joseph Luchesi in the Weißkirchen choral society and gymnastics club, Mährischer Correspondent 1862
links.source: Mährischer Correspondent (Brünn), newspaper (ANNO, Österreichische Nationalbibliothek)
links.summary: Two reports from Mährisch Weißkirchen (Hranice) in the Brünn newspaper Mährischer Correspondent. On 12 October 1862 Joseph Luchesi was re-elected secretary (Schriftführer) of the men's choral society (Männergesangverein), together with Gustav Mella; he had been secretary and committee member since its founding. On 8 October 1862 he was one of eight men who formed a provisional committee to found a gymnastics club (Turnverein) with a fire brigade. Shows Josef Jr living in Weißkirchen in 1862 (fills part of the 1855–1885 gap); Josef Sr would have been well over 70.
links.transcript:
Mährischer Correspondent, 1. November 1862, S. 11

Mähr. Weißkirchen, 18. October. [Orig. Corresp.] (Gesangverein.) Am 12. October d. J. ist beim hiesigen Männergesangvereine gemäß der Statuten die erste jährliche Neuwahl der gesammten Vorstandsmitglieder vorgenommen worden. … Zu Schriftführern, die Herren: Joseph Luchesi und Gustav Mella und somit blieben außer dem ersten Schriftführer Joseph Luchesi, der aber bereits auch schon seit den ersten Vorbereitungen zum Feste als Schriftführer und Comitémitglied fungirt hat, …

Mähr. Weißkirchen, 20. Oct. [Orig. Corresp.] (Turnverein.) Am 8. October d. J. haben hier nachstehende Herren, als: Wazlawik Franz, Wazlawik Heinrich, Blaschke Franz, Luchesi Joseph, Macher Joseph, Michel Joseph, Wehrle Friedrich und Mella Gustav ein provisorisches Comité zur Errichtung eines Turnvereines, womit die Feuerwehr und eine Turnschule verbunden sein soll, gebildet.

links.label: Ad by a Luchesi of Meidling (Vienna), Hauptstraße 36, 1889 — same address as the 1885 wedding witness
links.source: Neues Wiener Tagblatt (ANNO code nwg), newspaper
links.summary:
Advertisement (no. 4194, 28 Apr 1889): an old, well-known freight-forwarding business with a wholesale and retail coal trade in a larger industrial town in Moravia is for sale immediately on very favourable terms 'because of family circumstances'; enquiries to Luchesi, Meidling (Vienna), Hauptstraße 36.

Why it is attached here: the witness at Heinrich Luchesi's 1885 wedding in Neutitschein was read as '[Samuel?] Luchesi, [Privatbeamter?] Wien, [Mariahilf?] Hauptstr. 36'; this ad shows the address is almost certainly Meidling, Hauptstraße 36, so the same Vienna Luchesi (a close relative of Josef Jr and Heinrich, exact relationship unknown) lived there 1885–1889. The ad is NOT evidence of Josef Jr's death: it gives 'family circumstances', no estate/heirs/widow wording, the contact is in Vienna, and Josef Jr was alive in Feb 1889 as town secretary with no known link to a freight or coal business.
links.transcript:
Neues Wiener Tagblatt, 28. April 1889, S. 36, Anzeige Nr. 4194

Altes renommirtes Speditions- mit Engros- und Detail-Kohlengeschäft ist in einer größeren Provinz- und industrie-reichen Stadt Mährens wegen Familienverhältnissen unter sehr günstigen Verhältnissen sofort zu verkaufen. Nähere Auskunft ertheilt Luchesi, Meidling, Hauptstraße 36.

links.source: Miriam Aistleitner, "Volksdeutsche", Tschechinnen und Tschechen. Perspektive einer Zeitzeugin: Eva Morton-Wolf
links.page: Zwischenwelt, August 2014, pp. 69–73 — original German text (scan)
links.summary: Interview-based article on Eva Morton-Wolf (born Eva Maria Julia Wolf, Vienna, 30 June 1928, the youngest of three children). Father Sigmund Wolf (Jewish, non-practising; social democrat; textile factory in Leipnik/Lipník nad Bečvou) and mother Frida née Luchesi both came from Neu-Titschein. Family moved from Vienna-Döbling to Brno (Lipová 48) in autumn 1937; Sigmund died 20 Feb 1938 in the Kaufmännisches Sanatorium, Vienna. Under the Nuremberg Laws the children were 'Mischlinge ersten Grades': Eva barred from school, brother Peter put to forced factory work, sister Charlotte made to work for a transport firm near Brno. Frida's brother owned the leading confectionery in Neu-Titschein. After 1948 the family lived two years in Vienna; Eva and her mother emigrated to Sydney (1950), where Eva married Ernst Morton (born Mondschein, a 'Dunera Boy'); the family returned to Vienna on 30 April 1978.

links.label: Background: Italian-speaking chimney sweeps in Vienna and the Habsburg lands (Steidl 2009)
links.source: Annemarie Steidl, "Rege Kommunikation zwischen den Alpen und Wien – Die regionale Mobilität Wiener Rauchfangkehrer"
links.summary:
Background (historical context — not a record of this family): Italian-speaking chimney sweeps in the Habsburg lands.

Where they came from: Most Italian-speaking sweeps in Central Europe came from poor Alpine valleys around Lake Maggiore — Centovalli, Verzasca, Vigezzo and Maggia (Ticino/Piedmont) and the Misox (Graubünden). Centovalli appears on a mid-16th-century map as the "Kämifegertal" (chimney-sweep valley). The first sweeps in Vienna and other large Central European towns came from northern Italy, Ticino, Savoy, Piedmont and Graubünden.

How the trade worked (Steidl, on Vienna): A master's business was hereditary and saleable and tied to a fixed sweeping district (Kehrbezirk), which let migrant families nearly monopolise the trade. Guild rules allowed widows to continue or pass on a business. Whole families ran it over generations (e.g. ~30 masters from the Martinola/Martinolli family, ~28 from the Toscano family of Mesocco). About 11% of apprentices recorded in Vienna (1740–1897) came from the Bohemian lands, and the network reached Brünn (Brno). By the 19th century many masters were born locally, as businesses passed to second- and third-generation heirs. Much of the climbing work was done by boys of about 8–12.

Relevance to the Luchesis: Franz Luchesi was a chimney sweep (1812); his son Josef married in 1812 Katharina, a chimney sweep's widow running Kanitz house no. 117 — the pattern of a journeyman marrying into a widow's business described above — and became master chimney sweep in Kanitz, followed by his son Emanuel. Caution: the Moravian part is inferred from studies of Vienna; no direct evidence yet of where the Luchesis came from (the surname literally means 'from Lucca').

links.label: House no. 38, Na Můstku, Telč, today: the Luchesi family home 1777–1851 (street view)
links.summary:
Why this is house no. 38:
1. Telč's inner-town house numbers were given in 1770–71 and have not changed since (J. Mareček, Osídlení v Telči v 18. století, master's thesis, České Budějovice 2019, p. 87, comparing the 1775 urbarial survey, the 1792–1800 cadastre, the Stable Cadastre sketch and Rampula's 'Domy v Telči').
2. The same thesis puts houses nos. 33–38 in a row running to the end of Na Můstku lane, off the north side of the square (p. 90; n. 607: 'Ulice Na Můstku. Domy čp. 35, 36, 37, 38.').
3. Today the house next door is Na Můstku 37, and this house carries the number 38 above its door.
4. The family is recorded at no. 38: Lorenz borrowed money in 1777 to build it and died there in 1779; Franz and Catharina's children were baptised there 1784–1797; their grandson Franz worked there as master chimney sweep in 1847–1851. In 1775 Lorenz was at no. 35, three doors along the same lane.
Open question: Franz's 1835 death entry and the town land register give the house as no. 28, 'formerly 38'. The thesis says the numbering never changed, so this still needs checking.

notes: Josef Luchesi Sr, c. 1790 – 5 Oct 1862, chimney sweep and later master chimney sweep (Rauchfangkehrermeister) and burgher in Kanitz (Dolní Kounice). Son of Franz Luchesi, chimney sweep in Teltsch (Telč). Married 13 May 1812 in Kanitz Katharina née Elsner, a chimney sweep's widow at Kanitz no. 117, and probably took over her late husband's business. Sons: Josef Jr (c. 1818/19) and Emanuel (c. 1822–1874). Earlier readings of his wife as 'Barbara née Ch…' were misreadings of 'Katharina née Elsner' (re-checked on the 1848 marriage and the 1848, 1851 and 1853 baptisms).

links.label: House no. 38, Na Můstku, Telč, today: the Luchesi family home 1777–1851 (street view)
links.summary:
Why this is house no. 38:
1. Telč's inner-town house numbers were given in 1770–71 and have not changed since (J. Mareček, Osídlení v Telči v 18. století, master's thesis, České Budějovice 2019, p. 87, comparing the 1775 urbarial survey, the 1792–1800 cadastre, the Stable Cadastre sketch and Rampula's 'Domy v Telči').
2. The same thesis puts houses nos. 33–38 in a row running to the end of Na Můstku lane, off the north side of the square (p. 90; n. 607: 'Ulice Na Můstku. Domy čp. 35, 36, 37, 38.').
3. Today the house next door is Na Můstku 37, and this house carries the number 38 above its door.
4. The family is recorded at no. 38: Lorenz borrowed money in 1777 to build it and died there in 1779; Franz and Catharina's children were baptised there 1784–1797; their grandson Franz worked there as master chimney sweep in 1847–1851. In 1775 Lorenz was at no. 35, three doors along the same lane.
Open question: Franz's 1835 death entry and the town land register give the house as no. 28, 'formerly 38'. The thesis says the numbering never changed, so this still needs checking.

links.label: Marriage contract of Franz Luchesi and Katharina Köhler, Telč 1780
links.source: Městské knihy Telč (Stadtbücher Teltsch) — Kontraktenbuch (MZA aron, apu 40849d7f), contracts fol. 212–237
links.page: Kontraktenbuch Telč, fol. 235–237 — Heuraths-Contract Frantz Lükessy / Katharina Köhler, 10 Nov 1780
links.summary:
Marriage contract of 10 November 1780 between Franz Lükessy, single, burgher master chimney sweep in Telč, and Katharina, legitimate daughter of Wenzl Köhler, burgher of Telč (mother Anna Maria Köhlerin). Dowry 1,000 fl. (200 fl. after the wedding, 800 fl. later); Franz pledges his chimney-sweep business and house as counter-dowry. Witnesses Johann Kohler, burgher, and Franz Teubschel, baker. Entered 15 Dec 1780.

CONFLICT: the Telč baptisms of Franz's children (1784–1797) give the mother as Catharina, née Hübsch ('Hübschin', 1793), with godparents Wenzl and Maria Anna Hübsch of Iglau. The matching first names (Wenzl, Maria Anna) suggest one surname may be misread, or Franz married twice. Not resolved.
links.transcript:
Kontraktenbuch Telč, fol. 235–237 (Lükessy Frantz) — transcription by James

Heuraths-Contract.
Kund und zu wißen seye hiemit Jedermännigl:, insonderheit aber allda wo es zu wißen von nöthen, daß heut endes gesetzten dato zwischen dem Hrn Frantz Lükessy ledig bürgerlichen Rauchfangkehrer alß Bräutigam an Einem, dann der Tugendsamen Jungfrauen Katharina des Herrn Wenzl Köhler hiesigen Bürgers u. Ehelich Tochter alß Brauth am Anderen Theil beschloßen, und getroffener Ehepacten worden.
Erstlich. Thuet Verlobte Jungfrau Brauth ihren geliebten Bräutigam Hrn Frantz Lükessy über die bereits auf sich ihro Vätterlichen Liebe, Beysteuer in Tausend Gulden Rein: zu ihme Bräutigam einzubringen, und außzuzahlen, nun pro Dote zwey Hundert Gulden gleich nach der Copulation, die übrige Acht Hundert Gulden aber nach Jahr und Tag, entweder ganz, oder aber nach und nach bey Abgang dero Eltern dieselben abtragen und zuzahlen, wogegen er Bräutigam zu einem gleichen, und wiederleglichen Gegengab Brautschatz dero angehenden Ehegattin ihro über das Zubringende, und in diesem Orthe zu setzen, daß wann sie Jungfrau Braut vor ihm sterben, ohne ihro auß der Ehe erzeugte Leibes Erben an ihn das abgehen soll, und weder Eltern noch Geschwistert das geringste
Folio 236v
davon ansprechen, außer der Braut zum Vattern, auf die übrige Achthundert Gulden aber keine anforderung mehr haben soll.
Andertens. Weiters gelobet der Herr Bräutigam seiner Braut alß gleichenmaßen auß Liebe und Treue das Rauchfangkehrer Gewerb zu ihro Gegengab alß auf sein eigenthümliches Hauß und alles Vermögen anzuweisen, und gegenseitig ihro zu guten gegen solchen Vorbehalt fl: Rein:
Drittens. Haben beyde Contrahenten in dem Stand sich dahin miteinander verglichen, daß wann eines oder das andere Theil von dieser Welt durch den zeitlichen Todt abfordern würde, so stehet dem anderen Theil frey, das Rückgelassene Vermögen völlig zu besitzen.
Schlüßlichen haben beyde Brauth Persohnen einander die Macht eingeräumet, gegenwärtigen Heuraths Contract mit Bewilligung des Löbl: Stadt Teltscher Magistrats in denen Stadt Büchern intabuliren lassen zu können. Alles getreulich und sonder Gefährde, zu dessen Festhaltung haben sich nicht allein beyde Contrahenten selbst
Folio 237r
237
unterschrieben, und ihre Pettschafften beygedruckt, sondern auch die unten benannten Herren Zeugen mit ihren eigenhändigen Unterschriften und aufgedruckten Pettschafften bekräftiget. So geschehen Stadt Teltsch den 10ten 9bris im Jahr 1780.
[L.S.] Frantz Lükessy bürgerlicher Rauchfangkehrer Meister.
[L.S.] Wenzl Köhler der Brauth Vatter.
Johann Kohler Bürger alß Zeig.
Anna Maria Köhlerin alß Ehegattin.
Frantz Teubschel Becker alß Zeig.
Ingross: cum Consensu Senatus Die 15ta Decembris 1780,
Consule Dno Francisco Müller
Jos: Veneta Synd:

notes:
Katharina née Hübsch, wife of Franz Luchesi, chimney sweep in Telč; mother of Franz Xaver (bapt. 12 Nov 1784), Marianne (6 Dec 1786), Johann Wenzl (11 Jan 1788), Josef Sr (19 Nov 1790) and Aloysia Katharina (30 Jul 1793), all at Telč house no. 38.
Maiden name: the 1793 baptism names the mother 'Katharina Hübschin' (= née Hübsch). The earlier baptisms give only 'Catharina'. Her family was from Iglau (Jihlava): Wenzl Hübsch — described as furrier (Kürschner, 1786; reading uncertain) and clothmaker (Tuchmacher, 1793), burgher of Iglau — was godfather to Marianne, Johann Wenzl, Josef and Aloysia, and Johann Wenzl was named after him; probably her brother or father. Still to find: her baptism and the couple's marriage (before 1784; not in the Telč town marriages 1774–1790) — try Iglau.

Possible conflict (17 Nov 2026): a marriage contract of 10 Nov 1780 in the Telč town books (Kontraktenbuch fol. 235–237) names Franz Lükessy's bride as Katharina, daughter of Wenzl Köhler, burgher of Telč, and Anna Maria Köhlerin. The baptisms of Franz's children call the mother Catharina (née Hübsch in 1793) and name Wenzl and Maria Anna Hübsch of Iglau as godparents. Either one surname is misread (Köhler/Hübsch) or Franz married twice. To check: Telč marriages Nov 1780 – early 1781.

links.summary: Estate division of 18 March 1780 among the heirs of the late Lorenz Lückessy, burgher chimney sweep in Telč. Under his will (made 1 Aug, published 3 Sep 1779) the son Franz took over house no. 38 for 800 fl.; after debts (incl. 14 fl. 38 xr. owed for the deceased son Philipp) 270 fl. 46 xr. was divided equally between the widow Barbara, Franz, Mathias (then at Freiberg in Steyermark), Johann (journeyman strap-maker, Riemergesell, abroad) and the daughter Katharina. Entered 14 May 1781.

links.label: Will of Lorenz Luchesi, Telč 1779
links.source: Městské knihy Telč (Stadtbücher Teltsch) — Testamentenbuch (MZA aron, apu 663030c0)
links.page: Testamentenbuch Telč, fol. 157 — nuncupative will of Lorenz Lückessy, 1 Aug 1779, published 3 Sep 1779
links.summary: Oral will of Lorenz Lückessy, burgher and chimney sweep in Telč, made on his sickbed on 1 August 1779 before witnesses Michael Jankowsky and Francz Czworžitzky; to be buried at St Anne's. Universal heirs: his wife Barbora and their children Matěj (Mathias), Franc (Franz), Jan (Johann) and Kateřina. The house (800 fl.) goes after two years to the younger son Franz, who must keep his mother at his table until her death (or give her the ground-floor parlour and 40 fl. a year). Published 3 September 1779 before the mother, son Franz and the witnesses.
links.transcript:
English translation by James (original not yet transcribed). Index: https://www.mza.cz/aron/apu/663030c0-bbd0-45e8-a32e-ec4b1c3d4c8c/dao/663030c0-bbd0-45e8-a32e-ec4b1c3d4c8c/file/0085945c-dd52-4e5f-a696-8b9d06bab419

Nuncupative [Oral] Will
Lorenz Lückessy
In the name of the Most Holy [Trinity], etc.
We, the undersigned, hereby testify that today, on the date and year written below, Mr. Lorenz Lückessy, burgher and chimney sweep of the town of Telč, requested that we visit him and hear his last will. Upon this request, we entered his house and found him lying in grave illness, yet nevertheless of sound mind, whereupon he presented his last disposition to us and declared as follows:
First: The above-named Mr. Lorenz Lückessy commends his soul to the Lord Jesus, that through His bitter Passion He may receive it into grace; and as for his body, that it be buried according to Christian-Catholic custom at Saint Anne’s, for which funeral he bequeaths:
* Funeral expenses: 16 florins, 0 kreuzers 
* For Holy Masses in that same little church of Saint Anne: 6 florins, 0 kreuzers 
* To the Literati Brotherhood at [the Church of] the Holy Spirit: 2 florins, 0 kreuzers 
* To the Confraternity of the Sacred Heart of the Lord Jesus: 2 florins, 0 kreuzers 
* For the Normal Schools: 0 florins, 30 kreuzers 
* For the Invalids [disabled veterans]: 0 florins, 30 kreuzers 
Second: Whereas the foundation and basis of every will is the appointment of a universal heir, so too he appointed as such his dear wife Barbora, together with the children proceeding from the present marriage, namely: Matěj [Matthew], Franc [Franz], Jan [John], and Kateřina [Catherine], to whom he left his house—apart from all household furnishings—appraised at eight hundred florins, I say: 800 fl. With the further stipulation, however, that she, the surviving wife and respective mother Barbora, shall remain the fully empowered mistress of the household for two years after his death. After those two years, however, he bequeaths that own house of his, appraised at 800 fl., to his younger son Franc Lückessy, who is to keep and care for his mother at his table until her death. Should they, however, in time be unable to get along together, he reserves for her, the mother, the small ground-floor parlor, and for her maintenance 40 fl. in money, which he, the son Franc, shall be obligated to pay her annually. And whatever shall remain after the payment of debts, the heirs shall divide among themselves in equal shares.
Third and lastly: That he, Mr. Lorenz Lückessy, disposed and declared his last will in this manner, we testify by the signature of our own names freely and with our seal, [being ready] should need arise to confirm the same by oath; which took place in the Town of Telč on the 1st day of August, Year [1]779.
[L.S.] Michael Jankowsky
[L.S.] Francz Czworžitzky [Čtvořický / Dvořický]
Requested witnesses
[Probate Note in Latin]: Published in full session before the Mother, the Son Franciscus, and the Witnesses on the 3rd day of September [1]779.
Under Mayor Mr. Konstantin Müller
Johann Veneta, Syndic [town clerk]

links.label: Background: Italian-speaking chimney sweeps in Vienna and the Habsburg lands (Steidl 2009)
links.source: Annemarie Steidl, "Rege Kommunikation zwischen den Alpen und Wien – Die regionale Mobilität Wiener Rauchfangkehrer"
links.summary:
Background (historical context — not a record of this family): Italian-speaking chimney sweeps in the Habsburg lands.

Where they came from: Most Italian-speaking sweeps in Central Europe came from poor Alpine valleys around Lake Maggiore — Centovalli, Verzasca, Vigezzo and Maggia (Ticino/Piedmont) and the Misox (Graubünden). Centovalli appears on a mid-16th-century map as the "Kämifegertal" (chimney-sweep valley). The first sweeps in Vienna and other large Central European towns came from northern Italy, Ticino, Savoy, Piedmont and Graubünden.

How the trade worked (Steidl, on Vienna): A master's business was hereditary and saleable and tied to a fixed sweeping district (Kehrbezirk), which let migrant families nearly monopolise the trade. Guild rules allowed widows to continue or pass on a business. Whole families ran it over generations (e.g. ~30 masters from the Martinola/Martinolli family, ~28 from the Toscano family of Mesocco). About 11% of apprentices recorded in Vienna (1740–1897) came from the Bohemian lands, and the network reached Brünn (Brno). By the 19th century many masters were born locally, as businesses passed to second- and third-generation heirs. Much of the climbing work was done by boys of about 8–12.

Relevance to the Luchesis: Franz Luchesi was a chimney sweep (1812); his son Josef married in 1812 Katharina, a chimney sweep's widow running Kanitz house no. 117 — the pattern of a journeyman marrying into a widow's business described above — and became master chimney sweep in Kanitz, followed by his son Emanuel. Caution: the Moravian part is inferred from studies of Vienna; no direct evidence yet of where the Luchesis came from (the surname literally means 'from Lucca').

links.summary: Oral will of Lorenz Lückessy, burgher and chimney sweep in Telč, made on his sickbed on 1 August 1779 before witnesses Michael Jankowsky and Francz Czworžitzky; to be buried at St Anne's. Universal heirs: his wife Barbora and their children Matěj (Mathias), Franc (Franz), Jan (Johann) and Kateřina. The house (800 fl.) goes after two years to the younger son Franz, who must keep his mother at his table until her death (or give her the ground-floor parlour and 40 fl. a year). Published 3 September 1779 before the mother, son Franz and the witnesses.

English translation by James (original not yet transcribed). Index: https://www.mza.cz/aron/apu/663030c0-bbd0-45e8-a32e-ec4b1c3d4c8c/dao/663030c0-bbd0-45e8-a32e-ec4b1c3d4c8c/file/0085945c-dd52-4e5f-a696-8b9d06bab419

Nuncupative [Oral] Will
Lorenz Lückessy
In the name of the Most Holy [Trinity], etc.
We, the undersigned, hereby testify that today, on the date and year written below, Mr. Lorenz Lückessy, burgher and chimney sweep of the town of Telč, requested that we visit him and hear his last will. Upon this request, we entered his house and found him lying in grave illness, yet nevertheless of sound mind, whereupon he presented his last disposition to us and declared as follows:
First: The above-named Mr. Lorenz Lückessy commends his soul to the Lord Jesus, that through His bitter Passion He may receive it into grace; and as for his body, that it be buried according to Christian-Catholic custom at Saint Anne’s, for which funeral he bequeaths:
* Funeral expenses: 16 florins, 0 kreuzers 
* For Holy Masses in that same little church of Saint Anne: 6 florins, 0 kreuzers 
* To the Literati Brotherhood at [the Church of] the Holy Spirit: 2 florins, 0 kreuzers 
* To the Confraternity of the Sacred Heart of the Lord Jesus: 2 florins, 0 kreuzers 
* For the Normal Schools: 0 florins, 30 kreuzers 
* For the Invalids [disabled veterans]: 0 florins, 30 kreuzers 
Second: Whereas the foundation and basis of every will is the appointment of a universal heir, so too he appointed as such his dear wife Barbora, together with the children proceeding from the present marriage, namely: Matěj [Matthew], Franc [Franz], Jan [John], and Kateřina [Catherine], to whom he left his house—apart from all household furnishings—appraised at eight hundred florins, I say: 800 fl. With the further stipulation, however, that she, the surviving wife and respective mother Barbora, shall remain the fully empowered mistress of the household for two years after his death. After those two years, however, he bequeaths that own house of his, appraised at 800 fl., to his younger son Franc Lückessy, who is to keep and care for his mother at his table until her death. Should they, however, in time be unable to get along together, he reserves for her, the mother, the small ground-floor parlor, and for her maintenance 40 fl. in money, which he, the son Franc, shall be obligated to pay her annually. And whatever shall remain after the payment of debts, the heirs shall divide among themselves in equal shares.
Third and lastly: That he, Mr. Lorenz Lückessy, disposed and declared his last will in this manner, we testify by the signature of our own names freely and with our seal, [being ready] should need arise to confirm the same by oath; which took place in the Town of Telč on the 1st day of August, Year [1]779.
[L.S.] Michael Jankowsky
[L.S.] Francz Czworžitzky [Čtvořický / Dvořický]
Requested witnesses

Under Mayor Mr. Konstantin Müller

Marriage contract of 10 November 1780 between Franz Lükessy, single, burgher master chimney sweep in Telč, and Katharina, legitimate daughter of Wenzl Köhler, burgher of Telč (mother Anna Maria Köhlerin). Dowry 1,000 fl. (200 fl. after the wedding, 800 fl. later); Franz pledges his chimney-sweep business and house as counter-dowry. Witnesses Johann Kohler, burgher, and Franz Teubschel, baker. Entered 15 Dec 1780.

Ehelich Tochter alß Brauth am Anderen Theil beschloßen, und getroffener Ehepacten worden.
Erstlich. Thuet Verlobte Jungfrau Brauth ihren geliebten Bräutigam Hrn Frantz Lükessy über die bereits auf sich ihro Vätterlichen Liebe, Beysteuer in Tausend Gulden Rein: zu ihme Bräutigam einzubringen, und außzuzahlen, nun pro Dote zwey Hundert Gulden gleich nach der Copulation, die übrige Acht Hundert Gulden aber nach Jahr und Tag, entweder ganz, oder aber nach und nach bey Abgang dero Eltern dieselben abtragen und zuzahlen, wogegen er Bräutigam zu einem gleichen, und wiederleglichen Gegengab Brautschatz dero angehenden Ehegattin ihro über das Zubringende, und in diesem Orthe zu setzen, daß wann sie Jungfrau Braut vor ihm sterben, ohne ihro auß der Ehe erzeugte Leibes Erben an ihn das abgehen soll, und weder Eltern noch Geschwistert das geringste
Folio 236v
davon ansprechen, außer der Braut zum Vattern, auf die übrige Achthundert Gulden aber keine anforderung mehr haben soll.
Andertens. Weiters gelobet der Herr Bräutigam seiner Braut alß gleichenmaßen auß Liebe und Treue das Rauchfangkehrer Gewerb zu ihro Gegengab alß auf sein eigenthümliches Hauß und alles Vermögen anzuweisen, und gegenseitig ihro zu guten gegen solchen Vorbehalt fl: Rein:
Drittens. Haben beyde Contrahenten in dem Stand sich dahin miteinander verglichen, daß wann eines oder das andere Theil von dieser Welt durch den zeitlichen Todt abfordern würde, so stehet dem anderen Theil frey, das Rückgelassene Vermögen völlig zu besitzen.
Schlüßlichen haben beyde Brauth Persohnen einander die Macht eingeräumet, gegenwärtigen Heuraths Contract mit Bewilligung des Löbl: Stadt Teltscher Magistrats in denen Stadt Büchern intabuliren lassen zu können. Alles getreulich und sonder Gefährde, zu dessen Festhaltung haben sich nicht allein beyde Contrahenten selbst
Folio 237r
237
unterschrieben, und ihre Pettschafften beygedruckt, sondern auch die unten benannten Herren Zeugen mit ihren eigenhändigen Unterschriften und aufgedruckten Pettschafften bekräftiget. So geschehen Stadt Teltsch den 10ten 9bris im Jahr 1780.

links.summary: Josephine cadastre of Telč (MZA Brno, D 6 Josefinský katastr, sign. 3546, 1787–1789). In the column of land types, under 'Parificirte Gärten und Teiche' (assessed gardens and ponds), Ried (field-name area) 'Orts Platz', an 'Obst Garten neben dem Ullitzer Teicht' — an orchard next to the Ulický pond, 191 square Klafter (Quadratklafter; about 690 m²). Per J. Mareček's thesis (Osídlení v Telči v 18. století, 2019, p. 89, n. 625), the Josephine cadastre records 'Ein Küchel Garten, dem Frannz Luchesy in die Stadt … N[umeru]m 38 gehörig', and the same orchard by the Ulický pond (topographic no. 97) appears in the 1792–1800 cadastre (SOkA Jihlava, AM Telč, inv. č. 117, Rampula Č 49). Transcribed from James's crop of the land-type column only; the owner's name and house number are in other columns of the page and are not in the crop. James matched the plot (no. 97) on the Stable Cadastre map, overlaid on today's satellite view: it is the triangle just west of today's Slavatovská street, south of road 112 near the Telčský potok. Measured on today's map it comes to about 676 m², close to the 191 square Klafter (about 687 m²) in the cadastre. Found by James, 18 Nov 2026.

House no. 38, Na Můstku, Telč, today: the Luchesi family home 1777–1851 (street view)
links.summary:
Why this is house no. 38:
1. Telč's inner-town house numbers were given in 1770–71 and have not changed since (J. Mareček, Osídlení v Telči v 18. století, master's thesis, České Budějovice 2019, p. 87, comparing the 1775 urbarial survey, the 1792–1800 cadastre, the Stable Cadastre sketch and Rampula's 'Domy v Telči').
2. The same thesis puts houses nos. 33–38 in a row running to the end of Na Můstku lane, off the north side of the square (p. 90; n. 607: 'Ulice Na Můstku. Domy čp. 35, 36, 37, 38.').
3. Today the house next door is Na Můstku 37, and this house carries the number 38 above its door.
4. The family is recorded at no. 38: Lorenz borrowed money in 1777 to build it and died there in 1779; Franz and Catharina's children were baptised there 1784–1797; their grandson Franz worked there as master chimney sweep in 1847–1851. In 1775 Lorenz was at no. 35, three doors along the same lane.
Open question: Franz's 1835 death entry and the town land register give the house as no. 28, 'formerly 38'. The thesis says the numbering never changed, so this still needs checking.

notes:
Father of Josef Luchesi Sr, named in Josef's 1812 marriage in Kanitz as 'Franz Luchesi, Rauchfangkehrer in Teltsch' (Telč, Moravia). Place name read as Teltsch on a close look at the 1812 entry (James/Claude, 15 Nov 2026); a strong but not certain reading.
Baptised 30 Mar 1754 in Telč as Franciscus Adalbertus, son of Lorenz (Laurentius) Luchesi, burgher master chimney sweep, and Barbara.
Update 15 Nov 2026: Franz lived in Telč from at least 1784 (house 38, town) — chimney sweep, burgher chimney sweep by 1788 — and died there on 2 Jan 1835 given as aged 83 (actually 80), burgher and master chimney sweep. Wife Katharina née Hübsch (of an Iglau family); children Franz Xaver 1784, Marianne 1786, Johann Wenzl 1788, Josef 1790, Aloysia Katharina 1793, Franziska 1797. His birthplace and marriage (before 1784) are still unknown.

links.source: Městské knihy Telč (Stadtbücher Teltsch) — Testamentenbuch (MZA aron, apu 663030c0)
links.page: Testamentenbuch Telč, fol. 157 — nuncupative will of Lorenz Lückessy, 1 Aug 1779, published 3 Sep 1779
links.summary: Oral will of Lorenz Lückessy, burgher and chimney sweep in Telč, made on his sickbed on 1 August 1779 before witnesses Michael Jankowsky and Francz Czworžitzky; to be buried at St Anne's. Universal heirs: his wife Barbora and their children Matěj (Mathias), Franc (Franz), Jan (Johann) and Kateřina. The house (800 fl.) goes after two years to the younger son Franz, who must keep his mother at his table until her death (or give her the ground-floor parlour and 40 fl. a year). Published 3 September 1779 before the mother, son Franz and the witnesses.
links.transcript:
English translation by James (original not yet transcribed). Index: https://www.mza.cz/aron/apu/663030c0-bbd0-45e8-a32e-ec4b1c3d4c8c/dao/663030c0-bbd0-45e8-a32e-ec4b1c3d4c8c/file/0085945c-dd52-4e5f-a696-8b9d06bab419

Nuncupative [Oral] Will
Lorenz Lückessy
In the name of the Most Holy [Trinity], etc.
We, the undersigned, hereby testify that today, on the date and year written below, Mr. Lorenz Lückessy, burgher and chimney sweep of the town of Telč, requested that we visit him and hear his last will. Upon this request, we entered his house and found him lying in grave illness, yet nevertheless of sound mind, whereupon he presented his last disposition to us and declared as follows:
First: The above-named Mr. Lorenz Lückessy commends his soul to the Lord Jesus, that through His bitter Passion He may receive it into grace; and as for his body, that it be buried according to Christian-Catholic custom at Saint Anne’s, for which funeral he bequeaths:
* Funeral expenses: 16 florins, 0 kreuzers 
* For Holy Masses in that same little church of Saint Anne: 6 florins, 0 kreuzers 
* To the Literati Brotherhood at [the Church of] the Holy Spirit: 2 florins, 0 kreuzers 
* To the Confraternity of the Sacred Heart of the Lord Jesus: 2 florins, 0 kreuzers 
* For the Normal Schools: 0 florins, 30 kreuzers 
* For the Invalids [disabled veterans]: 0 florins, 30 kreuzers 
Second: Whereas the foundation and basis of every will is the appointment of a universal heir, so too he appointed as such his dear wife Barbora, together with the children proceeding from the present marriage, namely: Matěj [Matthew], Franc [Franz], Jan [John], and Kateřina [Catherine], to whom he left his house—apart from all household furnishings—appraised at eight hundred florins, I say: 800 fl. With the further stipulation, however, that she, the surviving wife and respective mother Barbora, shall remain the fully empowered mistress of the household for two years after his death. After those two years, however, he bequeaths that own house of his, appraised at 800 fl., to his younger son Franc Lückessy, who is to keep and care for his mother at his table until her death. Should they, however, in time be unable to get along together, he reserves for her, the mother, the small ground-floor parlor, and for her maintenance 40 fl. in money, which he, the son Franc, shall be obligated to pay her annually. And whatever shall remain after the payment of debts, the heirs shall divide among themselves in equal shares.
Third and lastly: That he, Mr. Lorenz Lückessy, disposed and declared his last will in this manner, we testify by the signature of our own names freely and with our seal, [being ready] should need arise to confirm the same by oath; which took place in the Town of Telč on the 1st day of August, Year [1]779.
[L.S.] Michael Jankowsky
[L.S.] Francz Czworžitzky [Čtvořický / Dvořický]
Requested witnesses
[Probate Note in Latin]: Published in full session before the Mother, the Son Franciscus, and the Witnesses on the 3rd day of September [1]779.
Under Mayor Mr. Konstantin Müller
Johann Veneta, Syndic [town clerk]

links.page: Kontraktenbuch Telč, fol. 233–235 — Erbtheiliche Ausgleichung after Lorentz Lückessy, 18 Mar 1780
links.summary: Estate division of 18 March 1780 among the heirs of the late Lorenz Lückessy, burgher chimney sweep in Telč. Under his will (made 1 Aug, published 3 Sep 1779) the son Franz took over house no. 38 for 800 fl.; after debts (incl. 14 fl. 38 xr. owed for the deceased son Philipp) 270 fl. 46 xr. was divided equally between the widow Barbara, Franz, Mathias (then at Freiberg in Steyermark), Johann (journeyman strap-maker, Riemergesell, abroad) and the daughter Katharina. Entered 14 May 1781.

links.label: Will of Lorenz Luchesi, Telč 1779
links.source: Městské knihy Telč (Stadtbücher Teltsch) — Testamentenbuch (MZA aron, apu 663030c0)
links.page: Testamentenbuch Telč, fol. 157 — nuncupative will of Lorenz Lückessy, 1 Aug 1779, published 3 Sep 1779
links.summary: Oral will of Lorenz Lückessy, burgher and chimney sweep in Telč, made on his sickbed on 1 August 1779 before witnesses Michael Jankowsky and Francz Czworžitzky; to be buried at St Anne's. Universal heirs: his wife Barbora and their children Matěj (Mathias), Franc (Franz), Jan (Johann) and Kateřina. The house (800 fl.) goes after two years to the younger son Franz, who must keep his mother at his table until her death (or give her the ground-floor parlour and 40 fl. a year). Published 3 September 1779 before the mother, son Franz and the witnesses.
links.transcript:
English translation by James (original not yet transcribed). Index: https://www.mza.cz/aron/apu/663030c0-bbd0-45e8-a32e-ec4b1c3d4c8c/dao/663030c0-bbd0-45e8-a32e-ec4b1c3d4c8c/file/0085945c-dd52-4e5f-a696-8b9d06bab419

Nuncupative [Oral] Will
Lorenz Lückessy
In the name of the Most Holy [Trinity], etc.
We, the undersigned, hereby testify that today, on the date and year written below, Mr. Lorenz Lückessy, burgher and chimney sweep of the town of Telč, requested that we visit him and hear his last will. Upon this request, we entered his house and found him lying in grave illness, yet nevertheless of sound mind, whereupon he presented his last disposition to us and declared as follows:
First: The above-named Mr. Lorenz Lückessy commends his soul to the Lord Jesus, that through His bitter Passion He may receive it into grace; and as for his body, that it be buried according to Christian-Catholic custom at Saint Anne’s, for which funeral he bequeaths:
* Funeral expenses: 16 florins, 0 kreuzers 
* For Holy Masses in that same little church of Saint Anne: 6 florins, 0 kreuzers 
* To the Literati Brotherhood at [the Church of] the Holy Spirit: 2 florins, 0 kreuzers 
* To the Confraternity of the Sacred Heart of the Lord Jesus: 2 florins, 0 kreuzers 
* For the Normal Schools: 0 florins, 30 kreuzers 
* For the Invalids [disabled veterans]: 0 florins, 30 kreuzers 
Second: Whereas the foundation and basis of every will is the appointment of a universal heir, so too he appointed as such his dear wife Barbora, together with the children proceeding from the present marriage, namely: Matěj [Matthew], Franc [Franz], Jan [John], and Kateřina [Catherine], to whom he left his house—apart from all household furnishings—appraised at eight hundred florins, I say: 800 fl. With the further stipulation, however, that she, the surviving wife and respective mother Barbora, shall remain the fully empowered mistress of the household for two years after his death. After those two years, however, he bequeaths that own house of his, appraised at 800 fl., to his younger son Franc Lückessy, who is to keep and care for his mother at his table until her death. Should they, however, in time be unable to get along together, he reserves for her, the mother, the small ground-floor parlor, and for her maintenance 40 fl. in money, which he, the son Franc, shall be obligated to pay her annually. And whatever shall remain after the payment of debts, the heirs shall divide among themselves in equal shares.
Third and lastly: That he, Mr. Lorenz Lückessy, disposed and declared his last will in this manner, we testify by the signature of our own names freely and with our seal, [being ready] should need arise to confirm the same by oath; which took place in the Town of Telč on the 1st day of August, Year [1]779.
[L.S.] Michael Jankowsky
[L.S.] Francz Czworžitzky [Čtvořický / Dvořický]
Requested witnesses
[Probate Note in Latin]: Published in full session before the Mother, the Son Franciscus, and the Witnesses on the 3rd day of September [1]779.
Under Mayor Mr. Konstantin Müller
Johann Veneta, Syndic [town clerk]

Bought from Franz Kayser a house-lot in the Vorstadt hinter dem Wasser, Telč, with garden and 2½ Metzen of land, for 240 fl. Rh.
Bond of 40 fl. to Jan Jankovský secured on his house in the Předměstí za Vodou; signs as master chimney sweep (Mistr kominářský)

Will published before the town council of Telč, in the presence of the widow and son Franz
Borrowed 100 fl. at 4% from St Anne's church (Dean Anton Liška), mortgaging his 'bought and rebuilt' house no. 38 in Telč

links.label: Lorenz Luchesi buys a house in the Vorstadt hinter dem Wasser, Telč 1763
links.source: Městské knihy Telč (Stadtbücher Teltsch) — Kontraktenbuch (MZA aron, apu 40849d7f), contracts fol. 212–237
links.page: Kontraktenbuch Telč, fol. 212–213 — Kaufkontrakt 20 Apr 1763, Lorentz Lükessy (buyer) / Franz Kayser (seller)
links.summary:
On 20 April 1763 Lorenz Lükessy, chimney sweep (Rauchfangkehrer) in Telč, bought from Franz Kayser a house-lot in the Vorstadt hinter dem Wasser, between the houses of Mathias Karas and Paul Mayer, with a small garden and 2½ Metzen of arable land, for 240 fl. Rhenish (140 fl. down, 100 fl. in yearly instalments of 20 fl.). The debt was later paid in full and cancelled (note by town syndic de Castelli, fol. 213). English translation by James:

Be it known and understood hereby to everyone, especially to those whom it is necessary to know, that today on the date set at the end below, between Mr. Lukessy, chimney sweep at the Town of Telč, as Buyer on the one part, and Franz Kayser, as Seller on the other part, an honest, well-considered, and irrevocable purchase and sale contract was concluded and agreed upon, as follows:
Namely, First: The first-mentioned Franz Kayser sells his property [house-lot] situated here in the Suburb Behind the Water [Vorstadt hinter dem Wasser], between the houses of Mathias Karas and Paul Mayer, together with the small garden belonging thereto and arable land amounting to 2½ Metzen of sowing capacity, along with all fixtures fastened with rivets and nails thereon, for and at the price of 240 Rhenish florins (fl. Rhein.), I say Two Hundred Forty Rhenish Gulden, in the following manner: namely, the Buyer pays a cash down payment immediately upon valid and official execution of this contract of 140 Rhenish fl., while the remaining 100 Rhenish fl. [are to be paid] in annual installments of 20 fl., I say Twenty [Gulden], wherewith to continue paying off until the above-mentioned entire purchase price is completely discharged and paid in full, and shall be.
Secondly: On the other hand, the aforementioned Mr. Lorentz Lükessy and his heirs also promise, regarding the quota of old debts and claims hitherto resting upon Johann Paul, respective Father Kayser’s [estate], to keep his property free [thereof], as it is termed in law, and [from] burdens, so that he himself shall enjoy and hold the same with all rights and privileges, just as the previous possessors did.
Thirdly: Furthermore, [both parties] grant each other the authority to have the present purchase and sale instrument secured [entered] in the town books (Stadtbücher) with the consent of the Honorable and Most Wise Town Council of Telč (Stadt-Teltscher Rath). All faithfully, without deceit.
In witness whereof, and for constant observance, not only have both contracting parties signed with their own hands and affixed their customary seals, but also the Gentlemen Witnesses requested at the end (however without any prejudice to them all), done knowingly and by request.
Thus done in the Town of Telč on the 20th of April 1763.
[L.S.] Lorentz Lükessy
[L.S.] Frantz Kayser + + +
[L.S.] Joh. Langer
[L.S.] Mathias Sattler
[Cancellation & Receipt Note on Folio 213r]: On the 3rd [day], the foregoing Lückessy payment item of 240 fl. was paid out in the Town Chancellery and already settled in full; therefore, the 240 fl. was approved on the protocol and cancelled (deliret) upon the petition of the creditor Franz Kayser.
I attest in good faith, de Castelli, sworn Town Syndic.
links.transcript:
Kontraktenbuch Telč, fol. 212 (Lorentz Lukessy) — transcription by James

Kund und zu wissen sei hiermit jedermänniglich, sonderlich denen, so es zu wissen vonnöten, dass heut endes gesetzten Datums zwischen Herrn Lukessy als Rauchfangkehrer bei der Stadt Teltsch als Käufer an einem und Franz Kayser als Verkäufer am anderen Teil ein redlicher, wohlbedächtlicher und unwiderruflicher Kauf- und Verkaufskontrakt geschlossen und verabredet [wurde], wie folgt:
Nämlich erstens (1mo): Verkauft erstgedachter Franz Kayser seinen allhier in der Vorstadt hinter dem Wasser, zwischen dem Mathias Karas und Paul Mayer Häusern gelegenen Grund samt dazugehörigem Gärtlein und Acker per 2½ Metzen Aussaat, samt allen darauf stehenden niet- und nagelfesten Sachen um und für 240 fl. Rheinisch, sage zweihundertvierzig Gulden Rheinisch, auf folgende Weise: und zwar zahlt Käufer bares Angeld sogleich bei gültiger und gerichtlicher Ausfertigung dieses Kontrakts 140 fl. Rheinisch, die übrigen 100 fl. Rheinisch aber in jährlichen Terminen à 20 fl., sage zwanzig [Gulden], womit so lange abzufahren [fortzufahren], bis obiger ganzer Kaufschilling völlig getilgt und ganz bezahlt wird und soll.
Hingegen zweitens (2do): Gelobt auch der vorgemeldete Herr Lorentz Lükessy und seine Erben, [bezüglich] der bisher auf Johann Paul, respektive Vater Kayserischen Anzahl [Anteil] der alten Schulden und Ansprüche seinen Grund frei zu [halten], als [wie] es in den Rechten heißt, und [von] Bürden, so [dass] er selbes mit allen Rechten und Gerechtigkeiten, wie die vorigen Possessores [Besitzer], genießen und haben soll.
Ferner drittens (3tio): Gibt [man] sich einander die Macht [einzu]räumen, gegenwärtiges Kauf- und Verkaufsinstrument mit Bewilligung eines Ehrsamen und Wohlweisen Stadt-Teltscher Rates stadtbücherlich versichern zu lassen. Alles getreulich, sonder Gefährde.
Zu Urkund dessen und steter Festhaltung haben nicht allein beide Kontrahenten sich eigenhändig unterschrieben und ihr gewöhnliches Petschaft beigedruckt, sondern auch die zu Ende gebetenen Herren Zeugen (jedoch ihnen allen ohne Nachteil) geschehen wissend und gebeten.
So geschehen Stadt Teltsch, den 20. Aprilis 1763.
[L.S.] Lorentz Lükessy.
[L.S.] Franz Kayser + + +
[L.S.] Joh. Langer.
[L.S.] Mathias Sattler.
213 (Löschungsvermerk)
Den 3. [Tag] ist die vorstehende Lükessysche Geld-Post à 240 fl. in der Stadtkanzlei ausgezahlt und bereits vergnügt [beglichen worden], daher per 240 fl. auf Protokoll bewilligt und deliret [gelöscht] ad petitum creditoris [auf Ersuchen des Gläubigers] Franz Kayser.
Testor in fidem [Ich bezeuge dies in gutem Glauben], de Castelli, Syndicus Civitatis juratus [geschworener Stadtsyndikus]

links.label: Lorenz Luchesi's bond to Jan Jankovský, Telč 1767
links.source: Městské knihy Telč (Stadtbücher Teltsch) — kniha dlužních úpisů / Schuldbriefe (MZA aron, apu 08ce0807)
links.page: Telč town book — bond (Schuldbrief) of Lorentz Lükessy to Jan Jankovský, 26 Mar 1767
links.summary: On 26 March 1767 Lorenz Lükessy, master chimney sweep (mistr kominářský), acknowledged a debt of 40 fl. at 4% to Jan Jankovský, arising from a settlement with his wife Barbora, secured on all his property and in particular his house in the suburb beyond the water (Předměstí za Vodou). Entered in the town book 31 May 1767.
links.transcript:
English translation by James (original in Czech; not yet transcribed):

Lorentz Lückessy.
I, the undersigned, by this my present bond, in the best and most enduring manner possible, make known that by reason of a fair and complete settlement between myself and my wife Barbora, I truly remain indebted in the amount of 40 fl., forty Rhenish florins, specifically to Mr. Jan Jankovský, which 40 fl.—together with 4 percent annual interest for him and his heirs on the aforementioned sum of 40 fl., as well as whatever interest accrues in the future up to the time of repayment—I obligate myself to render and pay back to him properly and in full.
And so that my creditor may be all the more secure, I hereby designate to him as a true mortgage and pledge all of my property in genere and in specie [in general and in particular], and specifically my own house situated in the Suburb Beyond the Water [v Předměstí za Vodou]; and I likewise establish that should any loss arise for him requiring compensation, he may duly recover against it [the house] and obtain full satisfaction in accordance with this bond.
In proof of this document, for greater credence and certainty, I sign with my own hand and affix my seal; and for better authenticity, I have confirmed this bond before witnesses and caused their seals to be affixed through them. Done in the Town of Telč on the 26th day of March 1767.
[L.S.] Lorentz Lükessy
Master Chimney Sweep (Mistr kominářský)
[Registration Note in Latin]: Entered into the register with the consent of the Senate [Town Council] on the 31st day of May 1767.
Under Mayor Mr. Joseph Ingerisch
Gabriel de Castelli, Syndic [town clerk]

links.label: Lorenz Luchesi borrows 300 fl. to build house no. 38, Telč 1777
links.source: Městské knihy Telč (Stadtbücher Teltsch) — kniha 131 (MZA aron, apu c3fccd71)
links.page: Telč town book 131 — Schuldverschreibung of Lorentz Lukesy to Johann Christoph Hebering, 300 fl. for building house no. 38, 18 Sep 1777 (ingrossed 8 Oct 1777)
links.summary:
Debt bond of 18 September 1777. Lorentz Lukesy, citizen of Telč, borrows 300 fl. Rhenish at 4% from Herr Johann Christoph Hebering [...] 'zu der guten Fraw' in Telč, for building ('zu Erbauung') the house no. 38 in the town of Telč, and mortgages that house and all his property. Signed by Lorentz Lukesy as debtor and by 'Anna Lukesyn'; witnesses Mathias Datl and Frantz Pumb. Entered in the town book with the consent of the council on 8 October 1777 (consul Franciscus Aibl). Earlier entered in this tree as the purchase of house no. 38 — corrected: it is a loan. Transcription and translation by James.

OPEN QUESTION: who is 'Anna Lukesyn'? Lorenz's wife is called Barbara/Barbora in 1751 (marriage), 1767 (bond), 1779 (will) and 1780 (estate division). Anna may be a misreading, a second name of Barbara, or another family member. Not resolved.
links.transcript:
Telč town book 131 (MZA aron, apu c3fccd71) — transcription by James

Lorentz Lukesy. Ich Endes unterschriebener urkunde und bekenne hiermit für mich meine Erben und Erbsnehmer, daß mir der Herr Johann Christoph Hebering [...] Zu der guten Fraw allhier in Teltsch auf mein geziemendes Ansuchen, und zu Erbauung des Johann Nepomischen in der Stad Teltsch Sub Numero 38. stehenden Haußes Ein Capital pr dreyhundert gulden rheinisch gegen darob üblichen 4. per centum Interesse gnädigst Vorgeliehen habe; Gelobe und Verspreche also hiernach für mich, meine Erben, und Nachkommen berührtes Capital dero 300 fl nach ein oder anderer Seits Vierteljährige Auffkündung hinwiederumb sambt denen etwa derlegten Interesse auffs bestlich zu bezahlen; Damit aber ein Herr Glaubiger, und jeder dieser Schuld-Verschreibung getreuer Inhaber respectu des Capitalis so wohl, als auch Interesse hinlänglich gesichert, und in keinen Weege geschädiget seyn möge; Als thue Ich hierwegen all mein Haab, Guth, und Vermögen in genere, in Specie aber obgedachtes Hauß des Numeri 38. in der Stad Teltsch pro Hypotheca reali judiciali expressa constituiren, und auf das beste hiemit Verschreiben; Wovon ich also in mindesten Versäumnißfall der Entrichtung sowol des Capitals als Interesse, dann etwan Verursacht- oder hernachstehenden Schaden und Unkosten halben via paratissima Executionis halten können und mögn; Verweigere mich, meine Erben, und Nachkommen dero aller Rechts Wohlthat sive Juris sive facti sit, Insonderlich der Exceptio non numeratae, aut non acceptae pecuniae, rei non sic vel aliter gestae, aut intellectae, doli mali, sinistrae persuasionis, und wie solche immer Nahmen haben, auch durch ein iezlichen Witz und Verstand erdacht werden können, Gestalten allen denselben per expressum und aufs aller feyerlichste renuncirt, stützen, noch formiren solle, Alles Getreulich, sonder aller List und gefährde: Macht und gewalt ertheillenden, womit diese meine gegenwärtige Schuld Verschreibung in meiner an- oder abwesenheit mit Bewilligung Eines Löblichen und Wohlehrsamen Magistrats auf meine Unkosten einverleibet, und ingrossirt werden könne; Zu wahren dann zeugnüß Urkund, und meiner höchster Bekräfftigung habe ich mich nicht nur allein eigenhändig unterschrieben, sondern auch die Endes stehende erbettene Herren zeugen zu gleicher mitfertigung allhier gebetten. So geschehen Stad Teltsch den, 18. Septembris 1777. Lorentz Lukesy als Schuldner, Anna Lukesyn, Mathias Datl als zeige, Frantz Pumb als zeige. Ingrossatum cum consensu Senatus die 8va Octob: 1777. Consule Francisco Aibl.

English translation by James:

Lorentz Lukesy. I, the undersigned, document and confess herewith for myself, my heirs, and inheritors, that Herr Johann Christoph Hebering [...] to the Good Lady here in Teltsch, upon my proper request, and for the construction of the Johann Nepomuk [?] standing in the city of Teltsch Sub Numero 38 house, has graciously advanced a Capital of three hundred Rhenish guilders against the customary 4 percent interest; I vow and promise thus hereafter for myself, my heirs, and descendants to repay the aforementioned Capital of 300 fl. after a quarter-yearly notice from one or the other side, back again together with any accrued interest in the best way; So that, however, a Herr Creditor, and every faithful holder of this debt-obligation is sufficiently secured with respect to the capital as well as the interest, and may in no way be damaged; Thus do I because of this expressly constitute all my belongings, goods, and wealth in general, but specifically the abovementioned house of Number 38 in the city of Teltsch as a real judicial mortgage, and in the best way herewith assign it; From which I therefore in the slightest case of default of the payment as well of the capital as interest, then any caused or following damages and expenses may be held via the most immediate execution; I waive for myself, my heirs, and descendants all their legal benefits, whether of law or of fact, Especially the exception of money not counted or received, of a thing not done thus or otherwise, or understood, of malicious deceit, of sinister persuasion, and whatever names they may always have, or can be devised by any present wit and understanding, expressly and in the most solemn way renouncing all of them, nor shall I lean on or form them, All faithfully, without any deceit and fraud: Granting power and authority with which this my present debt obligation in my presence or absence with the approval of a Praiseworthy and Honorable Magistrate at my expense may be incorporated and registered [ingrossed]; In true witness document, and my highest confirmation have I myself not only with my own hand signed, but also requested the undersigned Gentlemen witnesses to co-sign here. So happened in the City of Teltsch the 18th of September 1777. Lorentz Lukesy as debtor, Anna Lukesyn, Mathias Datl as witness, Frantz Pumb as witness. Entered into the registry with the consent of the Senate on the 8th of October 1777. Consul Francisco Aibl.

Nuncupative [Oral] Will
Lorenz Lückessy
In the name of the Most Holy [Trinity], etc.
We, the undersigned, hereby testify that today, on the date and year written below, Mr. Lorenz Lückessy, burgher and chimney sweep of the town of Telč, requested that we visit him and hear his last will. Upon this request, we entered his house and found him lying in grave illness, yet nevertheless of sound mind, whereupon he presented his last disposition to us and declared as follows:
First: The above-named Mr. Lorenz Lückessy commends his soul to the Lord Jesus, that through His bitter Passion He may receive it into grace; and as for his body, that it be buried according to Christian-Catholic custom at Saint Anne’s, for which funeral he bequeaths:
* Funeral expenses: 16 florins, 0 kreuzers 
* For Holy Masses in that same little church of Saint Anne: 6 florins, 0 kreuzers 
* To the Literati Brotherhood at [the Church of] the Holy Spirit: 2 florins, 0 kreuzers 
* To the Confraternity of the Sacred Heart of the Lord Jesus: 2 florins, 0 kreuzers 
* For the Normal Schools: 0 florins, 30 kreuzers 
* For the Invalids [disabled veterans]: 0 florins, 30 kreuzers 
Second: Whereas the foundation and basis of every will is the appointment of a universal heir, so too he appointed as such his dear wife Barbora, together with the children proceeding from the present marriage, namely: Matěj [Matthew], Franc [Franz], Jan [John], and Kateřina [Catherine], to whom he left his house—apart from all household furnishings—appraised at eight hundred florins, I say: 800 fl. With the further stipulation, however, that she, the surviving wife and respective mother Barbora, shall remain the fully empowered mistress of the household for two years after his death. After those two years, however, he bequeaths that own house of his, appraised at 800 fl., to his younger son Franc Lückessy, who is to keep and care for his mother at his table until her death. Should they, however, in time be unable to get along together, he reserves for her, the mother, the small ground-floor parlor, and for her maintenance 40 fl. in money, which he, the son Franc, shall be obligated to pay her annually. And whatever shall remain after the payment of debts, the heirs shall divide among themselves in equal shares.
Third and lastly: That he, Mr. Lorenz Lückessy, disposed and declared his last will in this manner, we testify by the signature of our own names freely and with our seal, [being ready] should need arise to confirm the same by oath; which took place in the Town of Telč on the 1st day of August, Year [1]779.
[L.S.] Michael Jankowsky
[L.S.] Francz Czworžitzky [Čtvořický / Dvořický]
Requested witnesses
[Probate Note in Latin]: Published in full session before the Mother, the Son Franciscus, and the Witnesses on the 3rd day of September [1]779.
Under Mayor Mr. Konstantin Müller
Johann Veneta, Syndic [town clerk]

links.label: The house beyond the water (Předměstí za Vodou), Telč: Stable Cadastre map over today's satellite view, Štěpnická street, house no. 260
House no. 38, Na Můstku, Telč, today: the Luchesi family home 1777–1851 (street view)
links.summary:
Why this is house no. 38:
1. Telč's inner-town house numbers were given in 1770–71 and have not changed since (J. Mareček, Osídlení v Telči v 18. století, master's thesis, České Budějovice 2019, p. 87, comparing the 1775 urbarial survey, the 1792–1800 cadastre, the Stable Cadastre sketch and Rampula's 'Domy v Telči').
2. The same thesis puts houses nos. 33–38 in a row running to the end of Na Můstku lane, off the north side of the square (p. 90; n. 607: 'Ulice Na Můstku. Domy čp. 35, 36, 37, 38.').
3. Today the house next door is Na Můstku 37, and this house carries the number 38 above its door.
4. The family is recorded at no. 38: Lorenz borrowed money in 1777 to build it and died there in 1779; Franz and Catharina's children were baptised there 1784–1797; their grandson Franz worked there as master chimney sweep in 1847–1851. In 1775 Lorenz was at no. 35, three doors along the same lane.
Open question: Franz's 1835 death entry and the town land register give the house as no. 28, 'formerly 38'. The thesis says the numbering never changed, so this still needs checking.

links.label: House no. 35, Na Můstku, Telč, today: Lorenz Luchesi's house in 1775 (street view)
links.summary:
Why this is the house:
1. In the 1775 urbarial survey of Telč, 'Lorenc Lukesek', chimney sweep (kominík), is listed as owner of house no. 35, taxed as a cottager (chalupník). He was the only chimney sweep in the inner town (J. Mareček, Osídlení v Telči v 18. století, master's thesis, České Budějovice 2019, p. 101 and p. 97; source: MZA Brno, D 5 Urbariální fase, fascl. 19 Y).
2. Telč's inner-town house numbers were given in 1770–71 and have not changed since (same thesis, p. 87).
3. The thesis places houses nos. 35–38 on Na Můstku lane (p. 90; n. 607: 'Ulice Na Můstku. Domy čp. 35, 36, 37, 38.'). This house on Na Můstku carries the number 35 (with street number 2).
4. By 1777 Lorenz was building house no. 38, three doors along the same lane, where he died in 1779.

notes: Lorenz Luchesi, burgher and chimney sweep (civis caminarius) in Telč — so called in the baptisms of 1758 and 1763; his widow's death entry (1796) calls him a burgher master chimney sweep (bürgerl. Rauchfangkehrermeister). Spelled Lukesi, Lukezi, Luxezer, Luxesy, Luxeser, Luxesi and Luchesy in the Telč registers. Children with Barbara, all baptised in Telč: Mathias Joseph (7 Feb 1752), Franz Adalbert (30 Mar 1754, d. 1835), Philipp Jakob (29 Apr 1756), Bartholomäus (23 Aug 1758), Katharina Elisabeth (10 Nov 1763). Mathias Czach, an employee of the Telč estate, was godfather to every one of them. Died 17 Aug 1779 in Telč, house no. 38, aged 55 (born c. 1724) — 'Laurentius Luxesi, civis caminarius' (death book 6995, img 215). Still to find: his marriage to Barbara (before 1752), his origin, and any children after 1763 (book 6975 runs to 1768; images 248 and 301–443 not yet reviewed).
